defects.after: The whole-chip test runs bwx12 with `--bytes 256M` (a buffer of 256 MiB per thread) and `--stop common` [Ref9]. With `--stop common` all threads of an interval have one common deadline. One timed call of a kernel covers 2 MiB, and the thread reads the clock after each call [Ref8]. A thread ends its interval at the first clock read at or after the deadline. A call over 2 MiB runs 8192 passes of a 256 B loop, or 16384 passes of the `oldread` loop. So the instructions before and after a loop run once per 2 MiB.

defects.after: New entries: "-O3, -march=native, -pthread, -Wall, -Wextra, -std=gnu11: gcc flags. `-O3` is optimisation level 3. With `-march=native` gcc picks the instruction set of the machine that it runs on. `-pthread` links the thread library. `-Wall` and `-Wextra` enable warnings. `-std=gnu11` selects the C language of 2011 with GNU extensions [Ref18]." "-fno-tree-loop-distribute-patterns: a gcc flag. With it gcc does not replace a loop by a call of a library function such as `memset` [Ref18]." "-fno-ipa-icf, -fno-toplevel-reorder, -falign-functions=4: gcc flags. With `-fno-ipa-icf` gcc does not merge two functions that have the same code. With `-fno-toplevel-reorder` gcc keeps the functions in the order of the source file. With `-falign-functions=4` gcc aligns the start of a function to 4 bytes only [Ref18]. bwx12.c needs the last two flags to put each kernel at a chosen address modulo 64 [Ref15]." New Ref18: external source, the gcc 14.2.0 manual on gcc.gnu.org, pages Optimize-Options, AArch64-Options, Link-Options, C-Dialect-Options and Warning-Options.
defects.evidence: Undefined option names are the defect kind of rounds 2 and 4; I read the five pages of the gcc 14.2.0 manual, and lines 99, 146 and 459 of bwx12.c say why the build needs the last three flags.
